senses.gloss: focused only on the short term
senses.definition: Focused on what is close or immediate, so that you miss the wider or longer-term picture.
senses.caution: It is a strong criticism of someone's judgment. Aim it at a plan or a decision rather than a person, or it sounds like an insult.
senses.example: Cutting the training budget to hit this quarter's number is myopic, because we will pay for it in hiring next year.

cues.text: A manager wants to cut all research spending to make this quarter's margin look better, and you think it will hurt the company in two years.
You review a design that fixes today's bug but makes every future change harder, and you want to name the flaw in the thinking.
A team improves only its own metric and ignores how its change slows down three other teams.
A friend spends their whole bonus on a holiday even though their rent goes up next month.

distractors: Willing to change a plan as soon as new facts come in.
Too proud to accept advice from anyone junior.
Careful to check every detail before a decision is made.
Planning many years ahead, even at the cost of results this quarter, and explaining why to everyone.
Quick to spend money on new tools without asking whether the team will actually use them in practice.
